item.title: Sharp Gromov Hyperbolicity Constants for Cartesian Products of Finitely Many Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.24253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X=T_1\times\cdots\times T_k$, $k\ge2$, be a Cartesian product of finite nontrivial trees with unit edges, and write $d_i=\diam T_i$, $S=\sum_id_i$ and $M=\max_id_i$. We prove that the thin-triangle hyperbolicity constant of the geodesic realization of $X$ is \[ \Rips(X)=\min\Bigl\{\frac S2,\ S-M+\frac12\Bigr\}, \] and that the four-point hyperbolicity constant of its vertex metric is the value \[ \mathcal{P}(d_1,\dots,d_k) = \max_{E\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}} \min\left\{ \sum_{i\in E} d_i,\, \sum_{i\notin E} d_i \right\}. \] of the best two-way partition of the diameters. Both constants therefore depend only on the diameter vector, and their difference is governed by the partition imbalance $\eta$ of that vector: it equals $\eta/2$ when $M\le S-M$ and $1/2$ otherwise. In particular the two constants coincide if and only if the diameters admit a perfect partition, and their difference is unbounded. For $k\ge3$ the first formula exhibits a many-factor balancing phenomenon: several short factors can collectively balance the longest one and force the universal bound $\frac12\diam X$ to be attained. The proofs are self-contained and rest on an exact distance formula for the geodesic realization of $X$. For the $\ell_1$-product of the factors, i.e.\ the $\ell_1$-metric on the associated cube complex, we obtain $\Rips=\min\{S/2,S-M\}$, which identifies the half-unit above as a pure $1$-skeleton effect, and we show that the four-point formula holds for $\ell_1$-products of arbitrary $0$-hyperbolic metric spaces, in particular for weighted trees and $\R$-trees. We also treat products with unbounded factors and record algorithmic consequences.
item.dc:creator: Junior Michel, Anier Soria Lorente, Jean Marie-Vilaire

item.title: Dimension Thresholds for Relative-Error Representations of Finite Metrics in Pseudo-Euclidean Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite metric space with $N$ points admits an exact representation in a pseudo-Euclidean space of dimension at most $N-1$. We study the minimum dimension required for relative-error approximation of squared distances. Our main result gives an upper bound for arbitrary metrics in terms of local distance ratios: for $4/5<\varepsilon<1$, dimension $O((N/k)\log N+k\rho_k^4\log N/(\varepsilon-4/5)^2)$ suffices, where $\rho_k$ is the largest ratio, over all points, between the distance to the $k$th closest point (counting the point itself) and the nearest-neighbour distance. The proof combines a low-rank landmark approximation with a sparse correction controlled by its factorization norm. For metrics with distances in $[1,\Phi]$, where $\Phi\ge5$ is fixed, the worst-case dimension is $\Theta(N)$ for $0<\varepsilon<4/5$, lies between $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ and $O(\sqrt N\log N)$ for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, and is $\Theta(\log N)$ for $\varepsilon>(\Phi^2-1)/(\Phi^2+1)$. For $\Phi>5$, an intermediate range remains without matching bounds. Sign-pattern counting yields the $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ lower bound for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, while Hadamard matrices give explicit linear lower bounds for $\varepsilon<4/5$ via a known approximate-rank estimate. We also construct configurations with null squared intervals whose minimum representation dimension remains $N-1$ for every $\varepsilon<1$. Finally, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<3/5$, we show that the quadratic dependence on the parameter $C$ in the dimension bound derived from Deng et al.'s pseudo-Euclidean Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is necessary up to a logarithmic factor.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Muravya, Aleksandr Bespalov, Anna Vozianova

item.title: Every Extended Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov--Hausdorff Class
item.description: arXiv:2610.24279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{GH}$ denote the Gromov-Hausdorff class of isometry classes of nonempty metric spaces, equipped with the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, which is an extended pseudometric. We prove that every nonempty extended metric space is isometrically embeddable into $\mathfrak{GH}$. More precisely, for every nonempty extended metric space $X$, the embedding can be chosen so that all image points are represented by metrics on a common underlying set of cardinality $\max\{\mathrm{dens}\,X,\aleph_0\}$, where $\mathrm{dens}\,X$ denotes the density character of $X$. To establish this result, for every nonempty set $I$, we realize the space of all real-valued functions on $I$, equipped with the uniform extended metric, as a family of metrics on a fixed underlying set. Under this realization, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance agrees with the uniform extended distance between functions, including when this distance is infinite, and each resulting metric space is complete, uniformly discrete, and unbounded, with cardinality $\max\{|I|,\aleph_0\}$. When $I$ is countable, the representing spaces can also be chosen proper and of bounded geometry. We also show that, for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, there are exactly $2^\kappa$ clouds represented by metric spaces of cardinality at most $\kappa$, and that $2^\kappa$ of their cardinality-restricted parts are isometrically universal for all metric spaces of density character at most $\kappa$. Furthermore, every sphere of positive radius centered at a point of the constructed copies of $\ell^\infty(\kappa)$ in the zero-distance quotients admits isometric embeddings of all metric spaces of density character at most $\kappa$ and diameter at most twice the radius.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Fukano

item.title: Infinitesimally Euclidean metric surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the equivalence of several notions of infinitesimally Euclidean-like behaviour for metric surfaces appearing in the literature. We obtain in particular that metric surfaces with property (ET) are universally infinitesimally Hilbertian.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Lytchak, Elefterios Soultanis

item.title: Distributions of metric $n$-point invariants and applications to molecular evolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.26070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Datasets often arise as samples from a metric measure space whose geometry reflects the data-generating process. We introduce metric $n$-point invariants, defined as functions of the pairwise distances of $n$-point configurations, to study the geometry of such spaces. This provides a unified framework for existing concepts, such as the pairwise distance itself, the Gromov product, and Vietoris-Rips persistence diagrams. The distribution of a metric $n$-point invariant $F$ over random $n$-point configurations can be used to extract geometric information from the space and is obtained as the pushforward of Gromov's $n$-th curvature measure $\mu_n$ along $F$. Our main result is an explicit bound for the expected $p$-Wasserstein distance between $\mu_n$ and the empirical curvature measure $\hat{\mu}_{n}$ of finitely many sampled $n$-point configurations, and carries over to the associated distributions of Lipschitz metric $n$-point invariants. From this we derive the sample size needed to achieve a prescribed accuracy and level of confidence in the approximation of the curvature measure. As an application, we use metric $n$-point invariants to study molecular evolution. We describe how site-wise nucleotide frequencies shape the corresponding distributions in Jukes-Cantor and Halpern-Bruno substitution models, and analyse five million SARS-CoV-2 genomes, revealing increasingly common failures of the four-point condition, constrained nucleotide accessibility consistent with the biased mutation spectrum, and rare cycles in persistent homology reflecting recurrent mutations across lineages. These findings demonstrate the potential of our sampling-based approach to the geometry of data as a scalable, phylogeny-free tool for detecting and quantifying evolutionary structure in large genomic datasets.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bleher, Mario G\'omez, Facundo M\'emoli, Maximilian Neumann, Andreas Ott

item.title: Depth based on translates of a convex body: geometry, floating bodies, and empirical theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.26108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, we study the $K$-depth of a point $y$ with respect to a probability measure $\mu$ by comparing the masses of translates of $K$ that fail to contain $y$. Its upper level sets are intersections of high-mass translates of $K$, and hence are convex and admit an exact representation as Minkowski erosions. We distinguish the closed core determined by the maximisers of the translation-mass function from the effective support on which the depth exceeds its unavoidable baseline. We establish continuity, affine equivariance, comparison with halfspace (Tukey) depth, and normal-cone and smoothness criteria. For uniform measures on convex bodies, the regions coincide exactly with the ball floating bodies of Sch\"utt, Werner and Yalikun; for positive continuous densities they coincide with the weighted ball floating bodies of Werner and Yalikun. For dilates $tK$, the depth converges to a depth generated by the tangent cones of $K$ as $t \to \infty$; for smooth $K$ this limit is Tukey's halfspace depth, whereas nonsmooth testing bodies can produce a genuinely different limit. The worst-case maximal $K$-depth is exactly $1/h_T(K)$, where $h_T(K)$ is the Helly number of the family of translates of $K$. Under a uniform interior rolling-ball condition and compact support and having zero mass on hyperplanes, the convergence to halfspace depth is monotone and uniform with an explicit error bound. If the density is bounded by $L$, then this bound is of order $O(t^{-1})$ and this order is sharp. We also record that the dependence on the testing body is not monotone in general, while Hausdorff perturbations of $K$ give stable depth functions and regions at regular levels. Finally, we prove uniform consistency and pointwise weak limits for empirical $K$-depth, including the non-Gaussian limit caused by nonunique active translates.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Molchanov, Stanislav Nagy

item.title: Finite convexification by Minkowski summation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact set and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact convex set. We study the problem of when there exists $\lambda>0$ such that the Minkowski sum $A+\lambda K$ is convex. First, we show that this finite convexification is equivalent to a uniform covering condition on the exposed sets of $A$ and $K$. We then show that another characterization is possible in terms of the covering radii of the iterated exposed sets after translating each exposed face of $K$ so that its relative centroid is $0$. In the case of convex polytopes, we show that it suffices to check the exposed sets in the first level of the iteration. We also study several special cases, such as strictly convex convexifiers, lower-dimensional convexifiers, strongly isomorphic polytopes, and the planar case.
item.dc:creator: Mark Meyer

item.title: Diamond Maximal Operators: Classification, Moduli, and Oscillation Envelopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study maximal averages generated by bounded cancellative kernels taking values in finite-dimensional real normed spaces, on Euclidean balls and on balls in a non-Archimedean local field with a fixed uniformizer. For angular kernels, pointwise domination of the full maximal operators is equivalent to factorization of their angular averaging maps, with the same optimal constant. Nonzero scalar angular comparison classes are therefore projective kernel classes. For angular kernels constant on a fixed finite measurable partition of the direction space, symmetric convex bodies classify exact norm measurements, Grassmannians parametrize nonzero classes under mutual domination, and positive semidefinite Gram matrices classify Hilbert-valued measurements. For general kernels, the closed convex hull of the averaging densities obtained from all scales and the dual unit ball is a complete invariant of the full maximal operator. A dilation example exhibits identifications of residue kernels beyond scaling and unit-coordinate changes. For nonzero radial residue kernels on bounded inputs, mutual domination is classified by the unit-circle zeros of filter polynomials, counted with multiplicity, with optimal constants given by the $\ell^1$ norms of convolution quotients. We identify the envelope over all normalized bounded cancellative kernels with the best local $L^1$ approximation by constants and prove quantitative convergence of residue envelopes as the resolution increases. Finally, the weights of the finite Fourier transform classify the one-level energy and the associated Carleson functional. This functional is equivalent to the $BMO_2$ seminorm precisely when every nontrivial additive character of the residue field is detected, and the weights determine the optimal comparison constants.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Mohajer

item.title: Thompson's groups are sofic
item.description: arXiv:2610.25415v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that Thompson's groups $F$, $T$ and $V$ are sofic. As a corollary, all of them are also hyperlinear and not permutation stable. The proof relies on an explicit construction of sofic approximations to $F$ and $V$. Moreover, the construction allows us to obtain effective quantitative bounds on the parameters of sofic approximations.
item.dc:creator: Maksym Chaudkhari, Kate Juschenko, Kyrylo Muliarchyk

item.title: Geometric and measure-theoretic characterizations of the measure-determining property of balls in metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The question of what structural properties drive the collection of open or closed balls to uniquely determine Borel probability measures on a metric space, the ball property, has a long history in measure theory. While various sufficient conditions have been known since the 1970s, and it was shown by Preiss and Ti\v{s}er (1991) that it holds for all separable Banach spaces, Davies (1971) constructed a famous counterexample that shows it can fail on compact metric spaces. It was only recently established in van Delft (2026) that metric spaces admitting an isometric Hilbertian embedding must possess the ball property. This article provides a comprehensive structural and measure-theoretic characterization of the ball property. First, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the ball property to fail: the collection of balls must possess sufficient combinatorial capacity, which we define as charged dyadic shattering. Second, by characterizing the ball property via $\lambda$-systems, we place classical vector space results within a unified context. Building on this to understand spaces that have the topological capacity but lack linear or geometric rigidity required to force ball-annihilating measures to zero, we relate the metric outer measure to the cylinder outer measure on countable products of Polish spaces, deriving necessary and sufficient measure-theoretic conditions for the ball property to hold. This allows us to derive a structural taxonomy on the decoupling of the metric outer measure from the cylinder outer measure. This is subsequently used to deconstruct Davies' counterexample. Finally, we introduce a minimal combinatorial generalization of the ball property, the $n$th order ball property, and show that such classes can fully recover measure determination in highly pathological constructions like Davies' counterexample.
item.dc:creator: Anne van Delft

item.title: Union of Translates of a Convex Body
item.description: arXiv:2610.25841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of calculating the volume of the union of translates of a strictly convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. When $K$ is a ball, it is possible to simplify the inclusion-exclusion formula by summing over only a small subset of all terms. This subset corresponds to intersecting cells in the Voronoi diagram of the ball centers. We prove that the same simplification is valid for every strictly convex $K$ if and only if $d\leq 2$. Moreover, in three dimensions and when $K$ is $C^4$, we use the Fubini-Pick affine invariant to show that the topological identity underlying this technique holds if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid.
item.dc:creator: Alec Shelley, Daniel Tartakovsky

item.title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
item.description: arXiv:2610.26119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.
item.dc:creator: Roope Anttila, Jonathan M. Fraser

item.title: Rigidity of Euclidean Convex Fillings for Ordinary Ambrosio--Kirchheim Mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.26477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove rigidity for compact integral current fillings with respect to ordinary Ambrosio--Kirchheim mass. Let $C\subset\R^n$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, $n\ge1$, and let $T\in\I_n(X)$, where $X=\spt T$ is compact. Suppose $\iota:\partial C\to X$ is an isometric embedding for the Euclidean chord metric and \[ \partial T=\iota_\#\cur{\partial C},\qquad \M(T)=\Leb^n(C). \] Then $\iota$ extends to a surjective isometry $I:C\to X$ satisfying $I_\#\cur C=T$. No map from the filling to the convex body is assumed.
item.dc:creator: Xianfeng Jiang

item.title: Counting Lattice Points in Translations: Uniqueness and Existence Results
item.description: arXiv:2610.26523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalizing a recent theorem by Higashitani et al. (Comb. Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a lattice polytope $P$ the function $\mathrm{t}_P$ is decomposed into homogeneous components $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$, similar to the Ehrhart polynomial. It is shown that the functions $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$ are simultaneous eigenfunctions of a family of linear operators introduced by Kubert and Lang in (Math. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. A structure theorem for the simultaneous eigenspace corresponding to the $(n-1)$st coefficient in the decomposition of $\mathrm{t}_P$ is obtained. This leads to an explicit description of the set of functions $\mathrm{t}_P$, where $P$ ranges over all lattice polygons, as well as to inequalities for the number of lattice points in dilated and translated lattice polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Ansgar Freyer, Georg C. Hofst\"atter

item.title: Curvature distributions and the Steiner formula for characteristic surfaces in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.26706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a new Steiner-type formula for smooth surfaces in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group. The main novelty is that we admit characteristic points, whose presence produces nontrivial singularities both of the distance from the surface and of its tubular neighborhood. Such singularities are reflected in the Steiner formula: the expansion up to a given order $N\geq 4$ of the volume of the $\varepsilon$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)$ of a surface $S$ is no longer polynomial, in general, taking the form \[ \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)) = \sum_{j=1}^3\alpha_j\varepsilon^j+\sum_{n=4}^N \left(\alpha_n+\beta_n\log\varepsilon\right)\varepsilon^n+o(\varepsilon^N),\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0^+ . \] More precisely, under a geometric stability condition on characteristic points, we prove that the first three coefficients are integrals over $S$ of locally integrable curvature densities, coinciding with those known in the non-characteristic case. A new phenomenon appears at order $4$, equal to the homogeneous dimension of the Heisenberg group, where logarithmic terms may occur. We show that the higher-order coefficients are naturally described by a distributional analogue of Federer's curvature measures, whose logarithmic components are supported on the characteristic set. We compute the fourth-order coefficients explicitly. The proof is based on different ingredients of independent interest: (i) an explicit formula for the cut time of homogeneous surfaces, (ii) a fine analysis of the normal exponential map through blow-ups, (iii) the study of the stability of the surface cut locus under perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barilari, Eugenio Bellini, Tommaso Rossi

item.title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet
item.description: arXiv:2610.26720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Meng Yang

item.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.26778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for H\"older potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Cantrell, Pablo Carrasco, Emilio Corso, Federico Rodriguez Hertz

item.title: Asymptotics of Constrained Quantization for Compactly Supported Measures
item.description:
arXiv:2505.10801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study constrained quantization of a compactly supported probability $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^D$ by codebooks in a nonempty closed set $S$. For $0<r\le\infty$, the constrained error $e_{n,r}$ is attained and satisfies $e_{n,r}\downarrow L_r=\|\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\|_{L^r(P)}$. Set $\Delta_{n,r}=e_{n,r}^r-L_r^r$ for finite $r$. A Borel nearest-point selector $T$ induces $\mu=T_*P$. Writing $q_{n,s}$ for the classical $L^s$ quantization error, we obtain $e_{n,r}-L_r\le2q_{n,r}(\mu)$ and $\Delta_{n,r}\le C_rq_{n,1}(\mu)$ for $1\le r<\infty$, with $C_r$ independent of $n$, and $\Delta_{n,r}\le2^rq_{n,r}(\mu)^r$ for $0<r<1$. Also, $e_{n,\infty}-L_\infty\le2c_n(E)$, where $E$ is the nearest-point image of $\operatorname{supp}P$ and $c_n(E)$ is its covering radius. For $1\le r<\infty$, a weighted power-growth condition with exponent $ eta>0$ on a fixed source set $F$ bounds $\Delta_{n,r}$ below by the classical $ eta$-power quantization cost of $
u_F=T_*(wP|_F)$. If $d
u_F=\widehat w\,d\eta$ for a compactly supported reference probability $\eta$ and $\widehat w\in A_p(\eta)$, $1<p<\infty$, then $\Delta_{n,r}\ge
u_F(\mathbb{R}^D)[\widehat w]_{A_p(\eta)}^{-1}q_{n, eta/p}(\eta)^ eta$. These comparisons yield bounds for the quantization dimensions defined by $e_{n,r}-L_r$ and $\Delta_{n,r}^{1/r}$, with distinct behavior at positive and zero baselines. Convex and uniformly prox-regular constraints supply the growth weights through their projection inequalities. Circle and lifted Cantor distributions give matching quadratic-excess rates, while rectifiable weighted projections give lower Zador estimates.
item.dc:creator: Chenxing Qian

item.title: Notes on uniform contractions of congruent balls
item.description: arXiv:2602.15352v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we obtain stronger results on uniform contractions of intersections and unions of congruent balls, thereby extending previous partial confirmations of the Kneser-Poulsen conjecture in these settings. In addition, we establish Blaschke-Santal\'o-type inequalities for r-ball bodies.
item.dc:creator: K\'aroly Bezdek

item.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
item.description: arXiv:2607.23453v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson

item.title: Pyramidal Compactification of Asymmetric Metric Measure Spaces via Adjoint Transport
item.description: arXiv:2608.01145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A quasi-metric measure space (qm-space) is a set with a directed distance whose symmetrization is a complete separable metric, together with a Borel probability measure of full support. Motivated by the problem of determining the pyramid limits of beta measures on forward Funk balls, we construct a compact metric space of pyramids of qm-spaces. The associated-pyramid map from the concentration-distance space of qm-spaces into this compact space is a $1$-Lipschitz topological embedding with dense image. As a secondary result, we prove that the box-distance space of qm-spaces is complete and separable.
item.dc:creator: Shigeaki Yokota

item.title: On the Log-submodularity for zonoids: from Mixed Volume inequalities to the Hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2608.14909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In convex geometry, a number of inequalities for the volume of coordinate projections of convex bodies share a common structural property. We formalize them as inequalities of log-submodularity type, providing a definition that stems from the notion of a submodular function. The Loomis-Whitney inequality and some of its generalizations are the most prominent examples. Some inequalities of log-submodularity type are valid for zonoids but not for general convex bodies. They have a natural meaning in statistics and information theory. We propose a new inequality of log-submodularity type for zonoids. In dimension 3, our inequality is equivalent to the log-submodularity conjecture for zonoids formulated by Fradelizi, Madiman, Meyer, and Zvavitch, which is true in dimension $3$ and false in higher dimensions. In contrast, our inequality is true in every dimension. We reduce our inequality to copositivity of a special polynomial, which we call the hypercube polynomial. For 4-dimensional zonoids, we verify the copositivity of the respective hypercube polynomial algebraically by providing a sum-of-squares certificate. In every dimension, a proof of copositivity of the hypercube polynomial that uses probability theory and well-known matrix inequalities has been produced by LLMs and brought to our attention. We present a detailed and easy-to-read version of this proof.
item.dc:creator: Gennadiy Averkov, Katherina von Dichter, Ivan Soprunov

item.title: The Spherical Hadwiger Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2608.27305v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the spherical Hadwiger theorem in every dimension: for $n\geq1$, every continuous $\mathrm{SO}(n+1)$-invariant valuation on all closed spherical convex sets in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ is a unique linear combination of the spherical intrinsic volumes $V_0,\ldots,V_n$. The same classification holds on sets contained in an open hemisphere, with unique continuous invariant extension to the full domain. We first classify simple invariant valuations by an independent induction on dimension. Averaging a signed cone identity gives the spherical volume term; the remaining terms are signed coning transforms that vanish by the lower-dimensional simple classification. A second induction, together with extension to non-proper sets, gives the general classification. The cone--sphere correspondence yields, for $d\geq2$, the corresponding classification on all closed convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without normalization at the zero cone. In both settings, $\mathrm{SO}$-invariance implies $\mathrm{O}$-invariance.
item.dc:creator: Suijie Wang, Shengguo Wu

item.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Distances Between Spheres: Asymptotics and Vietoris-Rips Coindex Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2609.07778v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $1\le m<n$, let $c_{m,n}$ be the infimum of the scales $r$ at which the Vietoris-Rips simplicial complex of the unit round sphere $\mathbb{S}^m$, equipped with its geodesic metric, admits a continuous odd map from $\mathbb{S}^n$. Previous work established the lower bound $\frac{1}{2}c_{m,n}\le d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\mathbb{S}^m,\mathbb{S}^n)$ through a quantitative Borsuk-Ulam theorem and raised the question of whether it is always sharp. We show that this bound can underestimate the distance by a factor arbitrarily close to two, the largest possible factor. Combining projective-code upper bounds for $c_{m,n}$ with lower bounds for $d_{\mathrm{GH}}$ obtained from obstructions to homomorphisms between Borsuk graphs, we obtain explicit finite-dimensional bounds. Along sequences of pairs $1\le m<n$, we have $c_{m,n}\to\frac{\pi}{2}$ whenever $\log n/m\to0$, while $d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\mathbb{S}^m,\mathbb{S}^n)\to\frac{\pi}{2}$ whenever $m/n\to0$. When both conditions hold (for example when $n=m^2$) the ratio of the distance to $\frac{1}{2}c_{m,n}$ tends to two. For each fixed $m\ge3$, the inequality is strict for all sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Sunhyuk Lim, Facundo M\'emoli, Qingsong Wang

item.title: Exponential improvements in Rado's covering problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.25288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $B^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball of unit radius. What is the largest constant $f(B^d) \in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $f(B^d)$ of the volume of $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T. Rad\'o in 1928, for axis-parallel squares in the plane; the author was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. The case of Euclidean balls was first considered by R. Rado in 1949. Until last year the best known estimates on $f(B^d)$ for unit balls where very far apart: \[ (1+\epsilon_d) 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2^{-d}, \] where $0<\epsilon_d=o_{d\rightarrow \infty}(1)$. Recently, the authors of this note observed that an exponential improvement on the upper bound follows from the Kabatiansky--Levenshtein spherical code bound, while the lower bound was improved by a linear factor by C.~Xie and G.~Ge (see arxiv:2608.09744). The current best estimates for large $d$ are \[ c \cdot d \cdot 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}, \] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Here we offer the first exponential improvement of the lower bound in almost 80 years, which narrows the gap to: \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}. \] Our method is constructive and yields a polynomial time algorithm for finding a disjoint sub-collection realizing the estimate. Moreover the same technique gives similar exponentially improved lower bounds for all symmetric convex bodies satisfying a uniform convexity assumption, e.g., $\ell^p$-balls for all $p\in (1,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Gian Maria Dall'Ara, Adrian Dumitrescu

item.title: The packing spectrum: interpolation between Hausdorff and packing dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10375v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a family of metric outer measures whose critical exponents form a packing spectrum interpolating between Hausdorff and packing dimensions. For analytic sets, we characterize each spectral value as the supremum of the Hausdorff dimension of a product with a compact testing set minus the testing set's upper intermediate dimension at the complementary parameter. The associated product bounds refine the classical Hausdorff--packing inequalities and can give exact Hausdorff additivity when both factors have distinct endpoint dimensions. Below the packing endpoint, we prove a variational principle in terms of windowed local mass exponents and sharp parameter estimates implying local Lipschitz continuity; a jump at the endpoint is possible. We characterize all attainable profiles by monotonicity, continuity below the packing endpoint, and a sharp upper right Dini-derivative bound. Every admissible profile is realized by a compact binary digit set whose uniform measure attains the finite-window and classical packing variational suprema. Complementary digit positions yield reflected upper intermediate-dimension profiles and a single factor attaining the Hausdorff product bounds at every parameter, with an Ahlfors regular product measure.
item.dc:creator: Peizhi Liu

item.title: Semidefinite programming bounds for distance distribution of spherical codes
item.description: arXiv:2309.13854v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multipoint semidefinite programming bounds for spherical codes use polynomials in several variables. We show how to obtain bounds for the distance distribution using a polynomial of one variable on a prescribed interval. The multivariate SDP supplies the required positivity; the sign and size of the univariate polynomial reveal the geometric consequences. We prove three- and four-point reductions and explain how to choose the polynomial to bound the number of pairs in a prescribed interval. Three-point experiments in dimension four illustrate this procedure, including nearly antipodal pairs, intervals near inner product $1/2$, and a local approach to the kissing number bound. As a further application, we extract a degree-six polynomial from the exact four-point construction of de Laat, Leijenhorst, and de Muinck Keizer. Its sign and four zeros give a direct description of the distance restriction underlying uniqueness of the $24$-cell.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Topological and Diophantine properties of lattice subset projections
item.description: arXiv:2606.01040v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper uses the Baire category theorem, the Riemannian manifold structure of Grassmannians, and the Khintchine Groshev theorem in Diophantine analysis, to relate properties of lattice subsets to those of associated subset of a Grassmannian.
item.dc:creator: Wayne M Lawton

item.title: The Geometry of Anisotropic Dilation for Optimal Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2610.09310v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How can structured transformations of data improve regularizer design for inverse problems? We address this question through anisotropic dilation, a direction-preserving map that rescales each point along its Euclidean ray by a positive profile on the sphere. Our analysis builds on a characterization of optimal regularizers within a broad Gibbs class, where the regularizer best matched to a distribution $P$ is determined by a direction-dependent radial summary statistic $\rho_P$. We show that anisotropic dilation acts explicitly and transitively on the space of radial summary statistics: any prescribed optimal regularizer in this class can be obtained by transforming an admissible source distribution using a single explicit profile. We characterize the resulting distributional orbits and establish conditions under which this control of regularizer geometry yields a weakly convex denoising formulation even when the original objective is not weakly convex. We also derive in closed form the profile that optimally adapts a fixed base regularizer to data. Its improvement over isotropic rescaling with respect to KL divergence is governed by a Jensen gap, for which we establish strict positivity under explicit conditions for several natural families of distributions. For jointly learning the base regularizer and anisotropic profile from samples, we establish finite-sample generalization bounds, with explicit rates when the logarithm of the profile is parameterized by linear feature models or sparse ReLU networks. Experiments on a controlled two-dimensional family and on MNIST denoising demonstrate that learning the anisotropic profile can improve reconstruction performance for both handcrafted and learned base regularizers.
item.dc:creator: Carson Newman, Oscar Leong
